trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum. It unlocks on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are all on your account, so there is nothing separate to hunt: work the list from the story trophies outward, keep the Missable Watch page open during your first run, and save the 100% completion grind for last. If it does not pop, one trophy is still outstanding — the tracker on this page will show you which.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Gone Fishing, the opening mission of the campaign. It plays out as the game's introduction, teaches the basic movement, driving and partner mechanics, and cannot be skipped or failed permanently — if a section goes wrong you simply retry the checkpoint. The trophy pops on the mission-complete screen, so just play the story and this one looks after itself.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing every mission in Chapter 1 of the story. Chapter trophies are strictly linear: follow the mission markers on the map, and the chapter closes once its final mission ends. Nothing in Chapter 1 is missable, but it is a good habit from here on to keep a rotating manual save, because later chapters contain the choices the Missable Watch page warns about.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish all of Chapter 2's story missions. The chapter leans into the duo's first big scores, so expect the wanted system and partner takedowns to be tutorialised here — a natural place to start practising for Gunslinger and Hot Together later. As with every chapter trophy, it is unmissable while you play the campaign in order and pops when the chapter's last mission wraps up.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 3. By this point the map and most activity types are open, so it is worth detouring between missions: try every activity once for Master of None, visit meditation spots for Positive Mental Attitude while you pass them, and start a collectible card set. The trophy itself is pure story progression and cannot be missed on a normal playthrough.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the endgame. Before you start its final missions, clear any stranger strands you care about and bank a manual save: the story narrows from here, and the finale is best approached with your side content done. The trophy pops at the chapter-complete screen and, like the other chapter trophies, needs nothing beyond playing the missions in order.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Gold for finishing the campaign's final mission. Go in stocked: full health and armour, upgraded weapons, and a manual save beforehand in case a choice near the end affects anything you still want from the open world. The trophy unlocks as the credits sequence begins. Afterwards the world stays open for the completion grind, so nothing else on this list needs to be finished before you take the finale on.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: A named-mission story trophy: complete Breakfast Run when it appears on the map during the early chapters. Named missions are part of the main campaign chain rather than optional side content, so following the story markers will bring you to it. It plays as a timed delivery-style drive; keep to the marked route, avoid trading paint with traffic, and the trophy pops at the mission summary.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist, one of the campaign's set-piece scores. Heist missions here reward a minute of preparation: approach quietly until the alarm is forced, keep your partner in cover during the holdout, and have a fast, durable car parked facing the exit for the escape. The trophy is tied to completion, not to your take or your approach, so any route through the mission earns it.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Child's Play. It is a character-driven mission in the campaign chain, so it arrives in order as you work through the chapters; there are no optional objectives tied to the trophy. If a chase or escort section gives you trouble, drop the difficulty for that attempt — the trophy does not care which settings you used, only that the mission ends complete.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. This one plays around a public event, so expect crowds, cameras and a wanted level you have to manage rather than outrun; use alleyways and a vehicle swap to break line of sight when the escape starts. It sits in the main mission chain and cannot be skipped, and the trophy unlocks on the results screen whatever your approach was.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Finish VCIA Takedown, the campaign's airport operation at Vice City International. Bring a suppressed weapon for the opening infiltration and something heavier for when it goes loud, and note the airfield layout while you are here — the free-roam trophy Catch Me If You Can also plays out at VCIA. The trophy is completion-based and unmissable in story order.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete Operation Savage Glory, a late-campaign set piece with a military flavour. Stock up on armour and explosives before the start marker, stick with your squadmates during the assault sections, and use Combat Focus generously in the open-ground fights — good practice for the Gunslinger trophy. As a main-chain mission it cannot be missed, and the trophy pops when the operation ends.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Gold for a full 100% completion stat. The completion counter covers the story, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and exploration tracked elsewhere on this list — but not literally everything in the game, so when you stall in the high nineties, compare the in-game completion checklist category by category rather than hunting at random. Do the story first, then strands, then collectibles; this is normally the last gold before the platinum.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunt events across Leonida — jumps, drifts, near-miss chains and the other scored feats the game logs as stunts. They are repeatable and scattered through the world, so the efficient route is variety: clear the marked stunt jumps district by district, then top up with freestyle stunts in a fast car on the causeways. Failed attempts cost nothing but time, and the counter in the stats menu always tells you how far you have to go.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Start every distinct activity type at least once: races, drone races, the shooting range, fishing, arcade games, bowling, meditation and the rest of the icons the map offers. You do not need to win or even finish most of them — registering a genuine attempt is what counts. Work the map legend from top to bottom; if the trophy does not pop, one activity type is still untested, and the newest icon type you have unlocked is the usual suspect.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold-medal every Shooting Range challenge — 42 of them across the ranges, grouped by weapon class. Learn one range at a time: gold is about accuracy streaks, not raw speed, so fire in controlled pairs, reload during target transitions, and memorise each course's spawn order before going for the medal run. Pistols and SMGs usually fall first; save the sniper and explosive courses for last, when the range rhythm is in your hands.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win one Top Fun drone race at each race location on the map — a win at every site, not every event. Fly the course once slowly to learn the gate order, then attack it: cut corners inside the gates, hold your racing line through the marked turns, and save your riskiest lines for the final sector. Locations you have already won are ticked on the map, so a quick legend check shows what is left.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — street, off-road, boat, air and drone events all count, but each must be a distinct event, so repeating your favourite circuit does not help. Bring the best vehicle class allowed, learn the first three corners of any new course (that is where the AI bunches up), and use slipstream on the straights rather than fighting through the pack. Spread the wins across the map and this finishes naturally alongside Top Fun.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Out-fish Cal in one of his fishing challenges. Cal is the benchmark angler at the fishing spots: accept his challenge, match the bait to the water you are on, and play the fish patiently — keep tension in the green while it runs and reel steadily when it tires. One challenge win is enough; if he beats you, the challenge can be retried straight away with what you learned about the spot.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Finish any one arcade cabinet game, start to credits. The cabinets sit in arcades and bars around Vice City; pick the shortest game on offer — the retro racers and shooters can usually be cleared in a handful of credits — and remember that inserting another coin to continue still counts as completing the same run. One full clear, on any cabinet, anywhere, earns the trophy.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's stranger strand by completing his final mission. Stranger strands unlock in stages as the story advances: do each of Andy's missions as his marker appears, and the finale becomes available once the earlier jobs are done. The strand trophies are independent of the main plot, so they can be cleaned up after the story — but finishing them as they appear keeps the Strangers & Freaks count ticking over.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the last mission of Kenton's strand. Kenton's jobs are water-flavoured, so expect boat work around the keys and the marina; keep a decent boat registered and your wanted level low before starting the finale, because a police chase on the water is harder to shake than on land. Like the other strand finales, it unlocks only after every earlier Kenton mission is complete.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's strand with his final mission. Billy's jobs revolve around riding solo — long highway runs and one-person errands — so a fast bike and a full tank of Combat Focus make the finale comfortable. Work his missions in order as they appear on the map; the final one only shows once the strand's earlier beats are done, and it also counts toward the eight strands needed for Strangers & Freaks.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete eight full stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida. A strand means the whole chain for one character, first meeting to finale — the named finale trophies on this list (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are five of them, so you need three more from the remaining strangers scattered across the state. Strands open up as the story progresses; if markers run dry, advance a chapter and check the map again.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission to close his strand. Randy's jobs are about moving product and keeping supply lines open, so expect delivery drives against the clock and the occasional ambush at the drop. Keep your delivery vehicle intact rather than fast — the cargo surviving is what matters — and finish his earlier missions first, because the finale marker only appears once the strand reaches it.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's strand by completing his final mission. Tyrone's appearances build toward one last job; do his missions in the order they unlock and the finale will be marked like any other strand end. It also counts as one of the eight completed strands for the Strangers & Freaks silver, so strand finales are always worth prioritising when they appear.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida — the quiet viewpoints marked once you first discover them. PowerPyx flags this trophy as missable: spots are scattered across areas the story passes through, and it is easy to finish the game with a few unvisited, so sweep each district's spots while the story has you there instead of leaving them all for the endgame. Sit through the full meditation animation at each spot; leaving early does not register the visit.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Track and hunt one unique animal at Bret's request. Bret's hunting strand sends you after a named, one-of-a-kind specimen rather than the common wildlife: follow his briefing for the animal's territory, approach downwind and crouched, and take the shot cleanly so the pelt stays presentable. Any single unique-animal hunt for Bret completes it; his other hunts are optional extras for cash and completion percentage.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Finish three full Collectible Card sets. Cards are hidden across Leonida in shops, bars, landmarks and out-of-the-way corners; a set completes only when every card in it is in your inventory, so collect by set rather than at random — finish the smallest sets first for an early completion, then work the big ones district by district. The collection screen shows exactly which cards each set still needs.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK photo spots at 100 different locations. Each marked viewpoint asks for a shot of a specific landmark or scene; line the landmark up inside the frame guide and the location registers. They cluster around tourist Leonida — beaches, the marina, downtown, the keys — so a single sightseeing lap with the map filtered to WAiNK spots knocks out dozens. Repeats at the same spot do not count twice.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete any 50 of the game's Challenges — the bite-size objectives listed in the challenges menu, from driving and combat feats to activity milestones. Most complete passively while you play (distance driven, headshots, near misses), so check the menu every few hours and deliberately finish the ones sitting at 80–90%. Fifty is well short of the full list, so you can ignore the few challenges whose style you hate.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, raise a genuine 4-star wanted level, then lose it completely and escape. The reliable method: commit crimes together in one car until four stars stick, then break line of sight — swap vehicles in an alley or parking garage, keep out of search cones, and let the stars drain. Both characters must be together for the escape, so do it in free roam with the duo in the same vehicle, not during a mission.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in a single unbroken spree with your partner, never letting the wanted level fully clear between them. Plan the route first: pick three stores within a short drive of each other, rob the first, keep stars on you while you drive to the second, and repeat. Your partner must be with you throughout, and if the wanted level drops to zero the chain resets — keep moving and keep the pressure on.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — a vehicle registers the first time you get in and drive it. Traffic variety differs by district, so rotate your hunting grounds: downtown for sports cars, the docks for trucks and vans, the marina and airport areas for service vehicles, and the rural north for farm and off-road machinery. Steal broadly rather than deeply and the hundred arrives quickly; rare spawns are not required.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Drop five enemies during one activation of Combat Focus, the slow-motion aiming ability. You need a crowd and a full meter: gang hideouts and the Pest Control operations are ideal setups. Charge the meter first, pick a weapon with a big magazine, line up your five targets before you trigger it, then sweep head to head without wasting shots on cover. If a run ends at four, reposition and retry — the ability refills fast in a firefight.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: At Vice City International Airport, take off in an aircraft you were never cleared to use — an unscheduled departure. In free roam, get airside (a gate jump or a ramp vehicle gets you over the fence), take any parked plane, and get airborne from the runway or taxiway. We flag it on the Missable Watch page because it is tied to a specific place and moment rather than general play; doing it in free roam as soon as VCIA is accessible is the safe play.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The official line is all you get: it gets hot inside a Rhino tank. This is the vehicle-mayhem trophy — get into a Rhino, survive the military response it attracts, and cause sustained havoc until the trophy pops. Rhinos are military hardware, so source one from a base incursion or a Savage Glory-style set piece, then keep moving: a stationary tank is a dead tank, and the heat you draw is the point of the exercise.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Clean out a jewelry store with zero detection: no alarm, no witness call, no wanted level. Scout the store first — note the clerk, the cameras and the back exit — then go in masked and quiet during a low-traffic hour, keep the clerk covered, smash and grab fast, and leave through the rear before anyone outside clocks what happened. If detection triggers, walk away and try another store rather than forcing it.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape the police after each one — a robbery you are caught or wasted during does not count. Vault jobs are the heavy end of free-roam crime: case the bank, bring explosives or a drill for the vault, post your getaway car a block away facing out, and lose the heat before returning. Different branches count, so work across the city rather than hitting the same bank five times.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Take down one armoured cash truck and escape with the money. Trucks run predictable routes between banks and depots; the clean method is to block the road ahead, use explosives or heavy fire on the rear doors, grab the cash cases, and be gone before the response escalates. One successful truck is enough — pick a quiet stretch of highway rather than downtown so your escape route stays open.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Uncover the whole map of Leonida. Exploration registers by area, so the fog lifts as you physically travel: drive every highway end to end, take a boat around the keys and coastline, and fly the gaps the roads miss. When the percentage stalls, the remaining fog is usually an island or a swamp pocket in the interior — a slow helicopter pass at low altitude over any grey patch finishes the job.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Hit an illegal operation run by every gang in Leonida — one robbery per gang, not one per location. Operations are marked once discovered: stash houses, chop shops and fronts. Learn each gang's territory from the map, rob one operation in each, and get clear; the trophy tracks gangs, so hitting the same gang twice only pays cash. These raids are also perfect setups for Gunslinger, with crowds of armed defenders in enclosed spaces.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have the cocktail-with-a-view moment on Ocean Beach: visit the beachfront bar on the Ocean Beach strip and order a drink where the terrace overlooks the water. We flag it as missable because it is a quiet, specific interaction tied to one spot rather than anything the story forces on you — nothing in the mission flow will remind you it exists. Do it on your first free-roam visit to Ocean Beach and it can never be forgotten.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Exit a vehicle showroom the loud way: through the glass, in one of its cars. Get into a display vehicle inside a dealership showroom, aim at the storefront windows, and drive straight out. The trophy wants the classic smash-through-glass exit, not the door, so pick a car facing the window line and commit to the throttle. Any showroom in the city works.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: A bowling trophy with a specific venue: the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Go there, play the lanes, and complete the follow-through the alley is known for — in practice, finish a game at this particular alley rather than any other in Leonida. Visiting every activity type for Master of None will bring you to bowling generally; this trophy wants this one address, so pin it when you are in the district.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The description gives you two clues: partnership and mass appeal. This is the duo's public-facing feat — build the pair's profile together by completing partner activities in public view, the kind the game tracks as the partnership's shared records. Play as a team in the open world rather than solo, chase the partner challenges the stats page lists, and this pops as their joint reputation peaks. It rewards playing the game as a duo instead of a lone wolf.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: A trophy about the story's decision points: 'choices made, for better or worse'. It is on our Missable Watch list because a choice-based trophy can depend on which way you decide when the game asks — the safe approach is to keep a manual save before any obvious branching moment (a sit-down, a phone call with two answers, a let-them-live-or-not beat) so the other branch is never more than a reload away. Play naturally, but save first.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: The clue is the description itself: the second time is the charm. This trophy is earned by failing at something once and succeeding on the retry — a race, a job, a challenge that went wrong first. We flag it as missable because a flawless player can play for hours without a natural failure to redeem; if it has not popped late in your run, deliberately take a fall in a quick event and win the immediate rematch.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Leonida's weird-event trophy: witness one of the game's strange phenomena out in the world — the kind of encounter that ends with the characters asking what just happened. These events live off the beaten path, typically at night in the swamps and the keys. Explore rural Leonida after dark, follow up odd lights and sounds rather than driving past, and stay for the whole encounter; leaving early means it never registers.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock down a group of pedestrians with a melee attack delivered from a moving vehicle — a drive-by, but with a melee weapon instead of a gun. You need a tight cluster of people and the right speed: too slow and it is just a brawl, too fast and you run them over instead of swinging. Sidewalk crowds outside nightlife spots in the evening are the natural setup; one clean pass through a group earns it.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder a cumulative $250,000 of Marked Bills through your fence contacts. Marked Bills come from the bigger scores — vault robberies, armoured trucks and gang operations — and they are worthless until a contact washes them for a cut. Make laundering a habit after every robbery rather than a final grind: drop the marked cash with a contact each time you pass one, and the quarter million accumulates quietly behind your other crime trophies.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend a cumulative $100,000 in shops — clothing, weapons and attachments, vehicle mods, haircuts, tattoos, food and property services all count, across every store type. It sounds like a lot until the mid-game, when a single fully modified car can eat a fifth of it. Spend naturally on gear you actually use, and if you are short late in the run, a luxury car plus a full mod package closes the gap in one visit.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy every garage property on the market. Garages appear for sale as you explore and as the story raises your profile; the property listings in the phone's real-estate app show what is still missing. They range from cheap lock-ups to a serious flagship space, so fund them with the robbery circuit — vault jobs and laundering from Dime on the Dollar pair naturally with saving for the last, most expensive garage.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles in the Scooter Bros app so they become yours — insured, trackable and deliverable. Any vehicle you can legally keep can be registered: buy some, and register found vehicles you like rather than ditching them. Register as you go instead of saving it up; ten slots fill quickly once you start keeping cars for the robbery circuit, and registered vehicles are also the safest getaway cars to rely on.
